Gross Description: Received in formalin, labeled "cervix 6 o'clock," are two fragments of tan white mucosal tissue, each measuring approximately 0.3 cm. Submitted entirely in one cassette.
Microscopic Description: Sections show squamous mucosa with marked architectural disorganization. Comment: The findings are diagnostic of CIN 2, a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion. Correlation with colposcopic findings and appropriate clinical management is advised.

Diagnosis: Kidney, native, biopsy; Lupus Nephritis, Class IV-G (A)

Light Microscopy Description: The specimen consists of two cores of renal cortex and medulla. Up to 28 glomeruli are identified for evaluation. All glomeruli show global, diffuse endocapillary and mesangial hypercellularity with neutrophilic infiltration. Multiple glomeruli contain wire loop lesions. There is moderate tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis involving approximately 30% of the cortex. No crescents or fibrinoid necrosis are seen.

Immunofluorescence Description:
IgG: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops (full house pattern)
IgA: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops
IgM: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops
C3: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops
C1q: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops
Fibrinogen: Negative
Albumin: Negative

Electron Microscopy Description: Electron microscopy confirms diffuse subendothelial and mesangial electron-dense deposits. Tubuloreticular inclusions are present within endothelial cells. There is approximately 50% podocyte foot process effacement.

Comment: The combined findings are diagnostic of active, diffuse global lupus nephritis. ISN/RPS 2003 Class IV-G (A)

The anesthetic medications administered during your procedure will continue to significantly impair your reflexes, cognitive function, and judgment for 24 hours. For your health and safety, it is absolutely essential that you and your designated caregiver read and strictly adhere to the following detailed discharge instructions.

CRITICAL SAFETY PRECAUTIONS (Next 24 Hours)

Your safety is our primary concern. The sedative effects are long-lasting and can create a risk for accidents and injury.

Driving and Transportation: You are legally and medically prohibited from driving any type of vehicle, including a car, motorcycle, or even a riding lawnmower, for 24 hours. You must be driven home by the responsible adult you have designated. Under no circumstances may you take a taxi, bus, or rideshare service alone.

Activity Restrictions: Do not engage in any strenuous or potentially hazardous activities. This includes exercising, going to the gym, or lifting heavy objects (anything over 10 pounds). Avoid activities that require balance and coordination, such as climbing over what stove.

Decision Making: Do not make any important or legally binding decisions. This includes signing contracts or documents, making significant financial transactions, or engaging in complex work-related discussions. Your judgment is considered impaired.

Impressions:
Normal Colonoscopy: A complete examination to the cecum was performed. The colonic mucosa was pink and healthy, with a normal vascular pattern throughout the visualized segments of the large intestine. There was no evidence of polyps, tumors, diverticulosis, inflammation, or other mucosal abnormalities.

Biopsy Information: No polyps were found, and no tissue samples (biopsies) were taken during your procedure. Therefore, you will not be receiving a separate pathology report.

Follow-Up Plan: Based on today's normal findings, your risk profile indicates that your next routine screening colonoscopy should be scheduled in 10 years. We will send a reminder to you and your primary care physician.
